identification.name: Acetal Homopolymer (Delrin / POM-H)
identification.common_form_notes: Widely available as extruded rod, sheet, and plate from plastics distributors (Delrin® is a DuPont/Dupont de Nemours trademark; equivalent grades: Hostaform C, Ultraform). Machines extremely well to tight tolerances and smooth finishes with standard cutting tools.
identification.notes: Acetal homopolymer (POM-H), sold as Delrin® by DuPont de Nemours. Semi-crystalline thermoplastic with high crystallinity (~75–80%), giving a sharp melting point, excellent dimensional stability, and low coefficient of friction. Distinguished from acetal copolymer (POM-C, e.g. Celcon) by slightly higher strength, melting point, and stiffness. POM is self-lubricating (PTFE-like wear behaviour) — excellent for dry-running bearings, gears, and cams without additional lubrication. Limitations: not suitable for strong oxidising acids, hot water or steam above 60 °C (hydrolysis), or prolonged UV exposure without UV-stabilised grades. Does not bond well with standard adhesives — use mechanical fastening or solvent welding where assembly is required. Continuous service temperature 90 °C (peak to 120 °C short-term). Very low moisture absorption (<0.2% equilibrium) gives excellent dimensional stability in humid environments.

typical_usage: Precision gears, cams, bushings, bearings, and slides in dry-running or lightly lubricated mechanisms; pump impellers and valve bodies for water and fuel service; threaded fasteners and stand-offs in assemblies where galvanic isolation is required; snap-fit components; food-contact parts (FDA-compliant grades available); electrical insulators.
